note: Built 17 October 2026 from data/topics/pizza.json to take the sushi searches that data/consensus/japanese.json's guide (best-japanese-restaurants-london) ranks for: 'best sushi restaurants london' (3.7), 'sushi restaurant london' and 'omakase restaurant london' (5 to 6), and a brief test for the bare query 'sushi'. The Japanese guide keeps the wider cuisine (ramen, izakaya, yakitori, kaiseki); this guide is only restaurants where sushi (nigiri, sashimi, handrolls or an omakase of them) is what the kitchen is known for. A Japanese or Nikkei room with a sushi counter among a long menu (Zuma, Nobu, SUSHISAMBA, The Aubrey) is mentioned once in a short section and is not ranked as a sushi restaurant. Counts are sushi-corpus only (trap 7): the Japanese corpus is not touched.

awardBodies.name: MICHELIN Guide (Great Britain & Ireland)
awardBodies.note: Has a real 'Sushi' cuisine filter for London. On 17 Oct 2026 it held three restaurants (Sushi Amamoto, Maru, Sushi Kanesaka), all Selected or one star; Sushi Kanesaka alone has a star (one, 2026). Further sushi kitchens sit under 'Japanese' and 'Japanese Contemporary' (Takahashi, Eel Sushi, Mayha, Tobi Masa, The Fuji Grill, Kioku by Endo, NIJŪ, Aki, Akira); their restaurant pages carry the distinction in JSON-LD 'award' with dateAwarded. No Bib Gourmand for sushi in London. Plain curl with no user agent works; a Chrome user agent returns an empty page. Umu has one star and Humble Chicken two, but Michelin's text for neither describes sushi.

awardBodies.name: The Good Food Guide
awardBodies.note: Server-rendered restaurant pages (/restaurant/<slug>/id/<n>) are readable but the ids cannot be guessed and search is client-side. Found through Google News RSS: the Kikuchi review (Very Good, 4 Dec 2025), the features piece 'Where to eat if you don't want to spend £400 on sushi' (14 Mar 2025) and 'First Look: Sushi Kanesaka' (15 Aug 2023). Other sushi reviews (Sushi Tetsu, Kurisu, Takahashi, Maru, Eel Sushi) could not be resolved to URLs.

awardBodies.name: Harden's
awardBodies.note: No sushi heading (the /sushi path returns a server error). Its London Japanese heading holds four restaurants; Pham Sushi and Sushisamba are the sushi ones.

editorialLists.name: Time Out
editorialLists.note: 'London's 20 Best Sushi Restaurants' (/london/restaurants/londons-best-sushi-bars), numbered 1 to 20, edited by Erin Niimi Longhurst. The 17 Dec 2025 news story naming Sushi Tetsu number one is the same list. Its Japanese guide is the same domain.

editorialLists.name: The Infatuation
editorialLists.note: Three guides on one domain: the 19 best sushi restaurants (not in score order), the 4 best omakase menus, and casual neighbourhood sushi spots. Ratings are printed per restaurant but the lists are not ranked.

editorialLists.name: Condé Nast Traveller
editorialLists.note: Gallery of 22, 1 March 2026. Includes Japanese rooms where sushi is one part of a wider menu.

editorialLists.name: Hot Dinners
editorialLists.note: Three guides: best sushi (27 entries, Jul 2025), omakase menus (Feb 2025), takeaway sushi (Aug 2025).

editorialLists.name: Evening Standard
editorialLists.note: The 2024 'don't cost a month's rent' list and David Ellis's five-star Eel Sushi review (Jun 2025). The 2018 list is outside the 36-month window.

editorialLists.name: Wallpaper*
editorialLists.note: Ben McCormack, ten picks, 7 Oct 2024, revised since.

editorialLists.name: House & Garden, The Week, Stylist, Vogue, Country & Town House
editorialLists.note: Japanese-wide lists; only their sushi-led entries are recorded.

editorialLists.name: Vittles
editorialLists.note: Jonathan Nunn's column on mid-range sushi (20 Sep 2024) is paywalled; the preview names Atari-Ya and Sagamiya.

editorialLists.name: The Nudge, Secret London, Washoku Guide
editorialLists.note: Independent and specialist lists. Washoku Guide lists 44 Japanese-owned or Japanese-chef sushi restaurants, unranked.

facetAxis.note: Sushi in London is five different meals. The axis is how the meal is served and what it costs, not the fish.

formatSection.title: Where the sources disagree
formatSection.note: The sources split on whether a sushi restaurant is the counter or the room. Time Out's ranked list leads with a seven-seat counter and puts a Battersea family room at 20; The Infatuation's list is neighbourhood a la carte rooms; Reddit threads are mostly about getting a seat at all. Keep to two sentences inside the first section.

knownGaps: SquareMeal's best sushi (24) and best omakase (16) lists, The Handbook's mid-priced sushi and omakase lists and Londonist's sushi bars list all return HTTP 403 to scripted requests, so none was read; The Times and Telegraph sushi lists are paywalled or blocked. The next pass should read them by hand and record them.
No TikTok creator is recorded: TikTok search cannot be read without a paid scraper and no reconstructed handle is acceptable (trap 5).

Tier E is Reddit only, counted as one domain however many threads name a restaurant; fifteen r/LondonFood, r/london and r/sushi threads were read, so thread counts are printed in the article text rather than in the Cited by line.
Kaiten is thin: Kulu Kulu is the only conveyor belt named by more than one source. Moshi Moshi (Liverpool Street) and Kurumaya are named by one Reddit commenter each.
Vittles' mid-range sushi column is paywalled beyond its preview; its full list of neighbourhood sushi-yas is not recorded.
No Bib Gourmand or other Michelin distinction exists for a London sushi restaurant apart from Sushi Kanesaka's one star; the Guide's 2026 selection no longer contains Endo at the Rotunda.
Taku and Sushi Amamoto share the Albemarle Street room; sources written before February 2026 name Taku. Left as two records.
Sources for Sushi Show, Hase-Ya, Sagamiya and the Ealing and Richmond neighbourhood sushi-yas are one or two voices each; there is no judged ranking for the cheap end.

Operator pages could not be read for Sushi Kanesaka (Dorchester Collection site returns a challenge page), Kurisu Omakase, Rai, Kikuchi, Iné, Nanahoshi, Uchi, Kumori, Kulu Kulu and Hase-Ya, so their prices and hours on the page are attributed to the Good Food Guide, The Infatuation, Time Out and Reddit. Rai and Iné are left off the page.
openVenueQuestions: Temaki - merged across Temaki Brixton (Brixton Village, named by CNT, Hot Dinners, the Good Food Guide, Wallpaper* and the Evening Standard) and the Mayfair site (named by The Nudge and in the Sheet as Temaki Mayfair). The Evening Standard reported the move; confirm with Rob that one record is right.

Taku and Sushi Amamoto - the same room on Albemarle Street, renamed in February 2026 when Shogo Amamoto became chef-patron. Not merged: sources written before the change describe Takuya Watanabe's Taku (Michelin star, opened 2022).

Dinings SW3 and Dinings Marylebone - two restaurants. The Infatuation lists both as separate entries; Reddit's 'Dinings in Marylebone' is the Harcourt Street one. The existing alias 'Dinings' -> 'Dinings SW3' in data/name-aliases.json sends a bare 'Dinings' to Chelsea.
Chisou - Mayfair (Woodstock Street) and Knightsbridge (Beauchamp Place) merged to the brand: The Infatuation names Knightsbridge, Condé Nast Traveller names Mayfair, Hot Dinners both.
Roka - four London sites merged to the brand; Time Out and Wallpaper* name the Charlotte Street original.
SUSHISAMBA - City (Heron Tower) and Covent Garden merged to the brand; the Sheet has two rows.
Eat Tokyo, Atari-Ya, Sushi Show - branches merged to the brand; sources name different branches.
Nobu - 'Nobu Old Park Lane' used where a source gave that address or the Mayfair site; Hot Dinners and Luxury London name Nobu's London hotel sites together.
Sushi Atelier - Fitzrovia, Shoreditch and St John's Wood; sources name the Great Portland Street original.

Endo at the Rotunda - closed by fire in September 2025 and not in the 2026 Michelin selection; ENDO (Chelsea) is a different room. Not merged. Endo at the Rotunda is recorded in the sources that named it before the fire and left off the page.
Sumi - the Notting Hill restaurant; a second SUMI in Marylebone was announced in July 2026 and is not recorded.

Cafe Japan (626 Finchley Road, Golders Green) - merged to Atari-Ya because Atariya's own site lists Atariya Cafe Japan among its restaurants at that address; Time Out names the same branch as Atari-Ya Golders Green. Atari-Ya's Swiss Cottage restaurant is a separate site under the same brand.

Moshi Moshi - recorded from one Reddit thread pair and the operator's own site; it is on the Liverpool Street station concourse and traded (food hygiene inspection May 2026), but its own pages carry no hours.
Chuo (Shoreditch monorail sushi) and Kurumaya (City) are named by Secret London 2024 and one Reddit comment; no food hygiene record or working operator page was found, so neither is on the page.
